Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:10:1.english: Together - So that I will not sit alone.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:13:1.hebrew: ע"מ - תנאה משמע, ולא בשכר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:13:1.english: On the condition - Implies a condition, and not as payment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:14:1.hebrew: ע"מ שירצה אבא - אביו של חתן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:14:1.english: On the condition that [my] father wants - The father of the groom.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:14:2.english: The father wants - The Gemara explains this:

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:14:3.hebrew: מלמדין וכו' - כדי לעקור את הקידושין למפרע, ולא תזקק ליבם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:14:3.english: One instructs, etc. - In order to uproot the betrothal retroactively, so that she will not be bound to a levir.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:1:1.hebrew: לא תסגיר - אזהרה לב"ד, שלא יסגירוהו לבעליו להשתעבד בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:1:1.english: You shall not deliver - [This is] a warning to the court, that they should not deliver him to his master to subjugate him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:1:2.hebrew: בלוקח עבד ע"מ לשחררו - דאי בשיחררו ובא להשתעבד בו, לא קרי ליה קרא עבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:1:2.english: In [the case of] one who acquires a slave in order to emancipate him - For if [it were speaking of a case where] he [already] emancipated him and came to enslave him, the verse would not call him a slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:1:3.english: When I will purchase you - [This] is an entity that has not [yet] come into the world.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:3:1.hebrew: משום איבה - איבת אחותה ואיבת בעלה, ואשארא כר"מ סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:3:1.english: Due to enmity - The enmity of her sister and the enmity of her husband; and regarding the rest [of the cases], he holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:5:1.hebrew: קונם שאני עושה לפיך - מעשה ידי יהיו לפיך כהקדש. אין בעלה צריך להפר, שאין נדרה חל, שהרי משועבדת לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:5:1.english: “Konam that which I make for your mouth” - The work of my hands shall be to your mouth like consecrated property. Her husband does not need to nullify [it], for her vow does not take effect, as she is obligated to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:6:1.hebrew: שמא תעדיף - על מעשה ידיה, יותר מן הראוי לו ויותר ממה שהיא חייבת לעשות לו. ובכתובות (דף סד:) אמרינן: מה היא עושה לו? משקל ה' סלעים שתי ביהודה, שהן עשר סלעים בגליל. ולכי אתיא העדפה — קדשה, אע"ג דלא באה לעולם בשעת הנדר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:6:1.english: Perhaps she will exceed - Beyond her handiwork, more than is fitting for him and more than what she is obligated to do for him. And in Ketubot (folio 64b) we say: What does she make for him? The weight of five selas of warp in Judea, which are ten selas in the Galilee. And when the surplus arrives, it becomes consecrated, even though it had not come into the world at the time of the vow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:6:2.hebrew: לעושיהם - למי שבראם. ומיהו, במידי דמשתעבדי ידיה לבעל, לא מצי לאקדושינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:6:2.english: To their Maker - To the One Who created them. However, regarding that which her hands are liened to [her] husband, she cannot consecrate them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:7:1.english: I will act for you as a laborer - With one day's labor.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:8:1.hebrew: והוא שנתן לה פרוטה - ואמר לה: ״התקדשי לי בפרוטה זו על מנת כו'״. והא אתא לאשמועינן תנא דידן, דבשכר דיבור או בשכר פעולה לא מקדשה, דישנה לשכירות מתחילה ועד סוף, ומלוה הוא. ולקמן מפרש היכי שמע לה ר"ל ממתני':
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:8:1.english: And this [applies only] if he gave her a peruta - And he said to her: “Be betrothed to me with this peruta on condition that...”. And this is what our Tanna comes to teach us: that with payment for speech or with payment for labor she is not betrothed, for wages accrue from beginning to end, and it is a loan. And later, [the Gemara] explains how Reish Lakish derived this from our Mishnah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:8:2.hebrew: שהרכבתיך - כבר נתחייבה לו, והוי מלוה גבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:8:2.english: That I had you ride - She has already become obligated to him, and it is [thus] a loan in her possession.

Rashi on Kiddushin 63a:9:1.english: That I will have you ride - And he [subsequently] had her ride.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:1:1.hebrew: כגון דכתב ליה לכשאקחך הרי עצמך קנוי לך מעכשיו - הכא משמע, דלמ"ד אדם מקנה דשלב"ל, מ"מ צריך הוא לומר מעכשיו. וכן משמע בפ"ק דב"מ (דף טז:), דקאמר התם: אמר רבא, "שדה זו לכשאקחנה תהא קנוייה לך מעכשיו". וקשה: דהא מילתא דרבי מאיר בסמוך גבי לאחר שאתגייר, לאחר שתתגיירי כו', דאמר ר"מ מקודשת, ולא קאמר דליבעי למימר מעכשיו! ואמאי צריך לומר בשדה ובעבד טפי מבגר? וכי תימא דהא דקאמר מקודשת היינו היכא דאמר מעכשיו, ואע"ג דליתיה בברייתא, וכדאשכחן בפ' האשה שנפלו (כתובות דף פב.) גבי "משוך פרה זו ולא תהא קנוייה לך עד לאחר ל' יום", ומוקי לה דאמר מעכשיו, ואע"ג דליתיה במילתיה — הא לא נהירא לומר כן; דמסברא מהני למ"ד אדם מקנה דשלב"ל כדבר שבא לעולם, דלא מצינו חלוק בדבר, ובדבר שבא לעולם לא מצרכינן לומר מעכשיו, דהא אמר במתניתין: "הרי את מקודשת לי לאחר ל' יום", לא בא אחר וקידשה — מקודשת, ואע"ג דלא אמר מעכשיו. והדרא קושיא לדוכתיה. לכך אומר ר"י דלא דמי: דלגבי קידושין היינו טעמא דלא בעי למימר מעכשיו, משום דסתם קידושין בכסף, וקנין מעות לא מתבטל, כדאמר לעיל: לא בא אחר וקדשה — מקודשת, ואע"ג דנתאכלו המעות; אבל הכא גבי שחרור של עבד וגבי שדה, דהתם רוב קניינם בשטר, ואם לא אמר מעכשיו ה"א אם נתקרע השטר בתוך הזמן העבד לא יהא משוחרר וגבי שדה נמי לא יהא קנוי לו, להכי נקט בשדה ובעבד לישנא דמהני בכל ענין, אפי' נקרע השטר, והיינו כשאמר לו מעכשיו. והר"ם פירש, דלהכי נקט מעכשיו גבי שדה ועבד, לאשמועינן דסבר כר"מ דאמר אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם, אע"פ שרוצה שיחול הקנין מעכשיו — קנה; דאי לא נקט מעכשיו, ה"א דאתיא אפילו כרבנן, וצריך לעשות קנין אחר השחרור. וא"ת: כיון שלא חל הקנין, אמאי הזהיר הכתוב שלא להסגיר עבד אל אדוניו, הא לא שיחרר ליה? מ"מ, כשפדוהו או קוניהו שליחותיה עבדינן, דניחא ליה דליקו בהימנותיה, כדאמרי' בפ"ק דב"מ (דף טו:) גבי גזל שדה וחזר ולקחה מבעלים הראשונים כו', ומסיק דניחא ליה דליקו בהימנותיה; אבל גבי קידושין לא שייך למימר הכי, ולכך לא בעי אמר מעכשיו. ומיהו קשה לפר"י, דפירש דמעכשיו מהני אפי' נתקרע הגט: א"כ ל"ל במשוך פרה זו מעכשיו לאחר ל' יום, דקא מוקי לה ר' יוחנן אפי' בעומדת באגם דמקום ראוי למשיכה, פירוש: ולא מיבעיא בחצירו, הא אפילו ברה"ר קיימא — קנה, כיון דאמר מעכשיו?! וי"ל: דר' יוחנן לטעמיה לעיל בפירקין (קידושין דף ס.), מעכשיו ולאחר ל' יום שיורא הוי, וה"ק: מעכשיו יתחילו הקידושין ולא יגמרו אלא עד לאחר ל' יום; וכמו כן אמר גבי מעכשיו דמשיכה. וכיון דלא קנה לגמרי, צריך שיהו בשעת גמר המשיכה במקום ראוי למשיכה; ומש"ה מוקי לה ר' יוחנן התם בעומדת באגם דראוי למשיכה, אבל ברה"ר לא. והא דקאמר הכא דאפי' נקרע השטר מהני הואיל ואמר ליה מעכשיו — אתיא כשמואל, דאמר לעיל (קידושין דף נט:): תנאה הוי. וצריך לדקדק אליבא דרבי יוחנן: איך אנו קונין שום דבר לאחר זמן, כגון שידוכים ושאר תנאים? דהא אפילו אמר ליה מעכשיו לא מהני לר' יוחנן אם חזר בו, או אם הוא קנין סודר, כיון שאין הסודר ביד הקונה בסוף הזמן, דהדרא סודרא למריה; דה"נ אמר (נדרים דף מח:) גבי ההוא גברא שרצה להקנות נכסים לבריה ע"מ שיהא בר בריה צורבא מרבנן (הוא), וקאמר התם דלא קני מהאי טעמא: דאימת קא קני — כי הויא בריה צורבא מרבנן, וההיא שעתא כבר הדרא סודרא למריה! ואמר הר"ם, דשמא ע"מ מהני אפילו לרבי יוחנן, ולא הוי שיורא אלא תנאי; ולכך טוב לומר: ע"מ מעכשיו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:1:1.english: For example, if he wrote to him: "When I purchase you, you are hereby acquired to yourself from now" - Here it implies that according to the one who holds that a person can transfer that which has not yet come into the world, nevertheless he must say "from now." And so it implies in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (16b), where it says there: Rava said: "[If one says,] This field, when I purchase it, shall be acquired to you from now." And this is difficult: For behold, regarding the matter of Rabbi Meir adjacent [to our sugya], regarding [one who says]: "After I convert," "[After] you convert," etc., where Rabbi Meir says she is betrothed, and he does not say that he needs to say "from now"! And why must he say [it] regarding a field and regarding a slave more than regarding a convert? And if you were to say that that which [Rabbi Meir] said, "She is betrothed," is where he said "from now" — even though it is not [stated] in the baraita, just as we find in the chapter [entitled] HaIsha Shenafelu (Ketubot 82a) regarding "Pull this cow and it shall not be acquired to you until after thirty days," which [the Gemara] establishes [as a case] where he said "from now," even though it is not [stated] in his words — this is not reasonable to say. For logically, according to the one who holds that a person can transfer that which has not yet come into the world, it should be effective like something that has [already] come into the world, as we have found no distinction in the matter; and with regard to something that has come into the world, we do not require [him] to say "from now," for behold, it says in our Mishnah: "You are hereby betrothed to me after thirty days," [and] another [man] did not come and betroth her, she is betrothed, even though he did not say "from now"! And the difficulty returns to its place. Therefore, the Ri says that they are not comparable: For regarding betrothal, this is the reason that he does not need to say "from now" — because standard betrothals are with money, and an acquisition made with money is not nullified, as it says above: "[If] another [man] did not come and betroth her, she is betrothed," even though the money was consumed. But here, regarding the emancipation of a slave and regarding a field, where most of their acquisitions are by document: and if he did not say "from now," I would say that if the document was torn within the time, the slave would not be emancipated and regarding a field it would also not be acquired to him. Therefore, regarding a field and regarding a slave, [the Gemara/Mishnah] used phrasing that is effective in any event, even if the document was torn, and that is when he said to him "from now." And the Ram explained that for this reason [the Gemara] used [the phrasing] "from now" regarding a field and a slave: to inform us that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir, who said that a person can transfer that which has not yet come into the world — even though he wants the acquisition to take effect from now, he acquires [it]. For if he had not used "from now," I would say that it follows even the Rabbis, and he would need to perform an acquisition after the emancipation. And if you say: Since the acquisition has not taken effect, why did the verse warn "You shall not deliver a slave to his master"? Behold, he has not emancipated him! [The answer is:] Nevertheless, when they redeem him or acquire him, we are carrying out his agency, for it is pleasing to him to stand by his word, as we say in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (15b) regarding one who robbed a field and went back and purchased it from the original owners, etc., and concludes that it is pleasing to him to stand by his word; but regarding betrothal, it is not applicable to say this, and therefore he does not need to have said "from now." However, it is difficult according to the explanation of the Ri, who explained that "from now" is effective even if the document was torn: If so, why do I need [the case] of "Pull this cow from now [to be acquired] after thirty days," which Rabbi Yoḥanan establishes [as applying] even when it is standing in a marsh, which is a place suitable for pulling — meaning, and it is not necessary [to say] in his courtyard, [since] why, even if it is standing in the public domain he should acquire it, since he said "from now"?! And one can say: Rabbi Yoḥanan is consistent with his own reasoning above in our chapter (Kiddushin 60a) that "[If one says,] From now and after thirty days," it is a reservation, and this is what he is saying: From now the betrothal shall begin, and it will not conclude until after thirty days; and likewise he said regarding "from now" of pulling. And since he did not acquire it completely, it is necessary that at the time of the conclusion of the pulling they be in a place suitable for pulling; and that is why Rabbi Yoḥanan establishes it there [as applying] when it is standing in a marsh, which is suitable for pulling, but in the public domain, no. And that which [the Ri] said here, that even if the document was torn it is effective since he said to him "from now," follows Shmuel, who said above (Kiddushin 59b) that it is a condition. And it is necessary to examine carefully according to Rabbi Yoḥanan: How do we acquire anything [that takes effect] after a time, such as in match agreements and other stipulations? For behold, even if he said to him "from now," it is not effective according to Rabbi Yoḥanan if he retracted, or if it is an acquisition by scarf [kinyan sudar], since the scarf is not in the hand of the buyer at the end of the time, as the scarf has returned to its owner! For so [the Gemara] also says (Nedarim 48b) regarding a certain man who wished to transfer property to his son on condition that his grandson be a young Torah scholar, and it says there that he did not acquire [it] for this reason: When does he acquire [it]? When his son is a young Torah scholar; and at that time the scarf has already returned to its owner! And the Ram said that perhaps "on condition" [al menat] is effective even according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, and it is not a reservation but rather a condition; and therefore it is good to say: "On condition [that it take effect] from now".

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג קונם מה שאני עושה לפיך - ול"ג "איני עושה", כיון [דבלאו] דמשועבדת לבעלה, לא מצית למיסר בקונם:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:5:1.english: This is the correct reading: "Konam what I make for your mouth" - And we do not read "I will not make," since [even] without [the fact] that she is bound to her husband, one cannot forbid [it] with a konam.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:6:1.hebrew: יפר שמא תעדיף - תימה: הלא אינו מיפר אלא דברים שבינו לבינה ועינוי נפש! וי"ל, דהא נמי דברים שבינו לבינה — שלפי שאי אפשר לצמצם ליהנות משלה מה שהיא חייבת לו, ואי אפשר שלא יהנה יותר מן הראוי לו, ויאסר אף בשאר מעשה ידיה; ולכך צריך להפר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:6:1.english: "He should nullify [it], perhaps she will exceed" - [This is] astonishing: Does he not nullify only matters between him and her and affliction of the soul? And it can be said that this, too, is a matter between him and her — for since it is impossible to be precise [enough] to benefit from hers [only] what she owes him, and it is impossible that he will not benefit from more than what is fitting for him, he would [consequently] be forbidden even from the rest of the work of her hands; therefore, he must nullify [it].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:6:2.hebrew: וידים איתנהו בעולם - והוי כמקדיש דקל לפירותיו, דמהני אפילו למ"ד אין אדם מקנה דשלב"ל. וה"ה דמצי לשנויי: שאני קונמות, דקדושת הגוף נינהו, כדמשני בפ' אע"פ (כתובות דף נט.):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 63a:6:2.english: "And hands exist in the world" - And [her declaration] is like one who consecrates a palm tree for its fruit, which is effective even according to the one who holds [that] a person cannot transfer [ownership of] something that has not come into the world. And similarly, [the Gemara] could have answered: Konamot [vows] are different, because they are [endowed with] intrinsic sanctity, as it answers in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 59a).
